ai.description: This 3–4 cm frog is lime-green with a distinct white lateral stripe. It features translucent skin on its belly and enlarged, pale-yellow toe discs adapted for life in lowland swamp forests.
ai.identificationRemarks: The *Mercurana myristicapalustris* is best distinguished by the distinct, fleshy, white-tipped webbing between its fingers and toes, which is absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: This frog inhabits evergreen swamp forests dominated by *Myristica* trees in the Western Ghats, typically found at low altitudes below 300 meters.
ai.behavior: The Myristica Lowland Tree Frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small insects among the canopy and foliage of its swampy forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Mercurana myristicapalustris* breeds during the pre-monsoon season (May–June), laying clutches of 100–300 eggs in small, shallow depressions within swampy forest floors.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Myristica Lowland Tree Frog is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in lowland evergreen forests and Myristica swamps below 300m elevation.
ai.callDescription: The Myristica Lowland Tree Frog emits a high-pitched, insect-like trill consisting of rapid, repetitive pulses while calling from vegetation in swampy forest habitats.
